plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-11 from the official Southern Utah University 2026-2027 General Catalog (current edition, catoid=28) Agriculture - Equine Studies Emphasis (BS) program page and its linked official degree map, 'Agriculture & Agriculture Education Degree Maps (2026-2027)', Equine Studies (Campus) tab, last updated/reviewed July 31, 2026. Semester placement is the university's official sample 4-year campus academic plan (SUU Program Maps, 2026-2027), which the source itself labels a guide only; students confirm specifics in Degree Works with a Student Success Advisor. The catalog prints Total Credits, BS Degree: 120, which the map matches exactly. Every term's courses sum to the map's printed term total (16/15/14/14/16/14/15/16) and the plan to 120. The catalog head reads 'Agriculture - Equine Studies Emphasis (60-61 Credits)': Agriculture Core 36-37 credits plus the Equine Studies Emphasis at 24 credits (17 credits of fixed courses, one 4-credit lecture/lab pairing, and a minimum 3-credit practicum/internship). The map exercises the catalog's options inside those ranges: the 4-credit chemistry pairing CHEM 1010 + CHEM 1015 (the catalog offers three lecture/lab pairings at 4-5 credits), COMM 4240 Technical Writing (one of the catalog's two writing options), the 4-credit AGSC/RANG Major Lecture/Lab Elective row for the catalog's 'Complete One of the Following' pairing block (AGSC 3030 + AGSC 3035, AGSC 3230 + AGSC 3235, or RANG 3600 + RANG 3605), and AGSC 4890 Internship at 3 credits for the catalog's Practicum/Internship Requirement (complete a minimum of 3 credits from AGSC 2950 Equine Practicum or AGSC 4890 Internship, each listed at 1-4 credits). Catalog titles are recorded where the map uses ampersands or shortens them ('Agriculture & Society', 'Animal Genetics & Breeding', 'Horse Science & Industry', 'Feeding & Nutrition of Horses & Livestock'). Per the catalog, major requirements must be completed with a grade of 'C-' or better and courses completed over 10 years ago are not accepted toward this degree.
